outcome: Give grid operations director / chief asset officer a governed method to improve hazardous span clearance backlog using satellite imagery, LiDAR surveys and line maps, with final decisions retained…
overview: Vegetation Encroachment Work Planning addresses resource allocation is planned in silos, producing avoidable delays and occasionally infeasible instructions in power and utilities operations. The first proof of value uses satellite imagery, LiDAR surveys and line maps. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is hazardous span clearance backlog, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: satellite imagery, LiDAR surveys and line maps; define hazardous span clearance backlog and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Grid Operations Director / Chief Asset Officer.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including replay disruption and edge cases with hard constraints enforced.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for hazardous span clearance backlog
